Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to surface a short mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to an executive briefing (EB) cadence so your execs can see progress and commit to procurement timing. Initial asks:

- Can you confirm who from Horizon will serve as the executive sponsor(s) for the EB sessions (name + title)?
- Do you have blackout days the week of May 10–14?
- We attached a first-pass MAP (MAP-draft-v1.xlsx) and a simple sponsor heatmap template — please add names/levels and any additional stakeholders.

Proposed EB structure (short):
1) Technical deep dive (internal engineers + product leads) — 60m
2) Exec briefing (CMO/CPO/CFO lane) — 30–45m with clear decision ask (budget/PO timing)
3) Final Q&A + procurement alignment — 30m

We can run two short EB slots the week of May 17 as a dry run and then the formal exec slot the week of May 24 to align on procurement. If that works, I’ll send a few proposed times and a one-page MAP timeline.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (stapled worksheet), sponsor-heatmap-template.csv

—Mina

Mina / team —

Nice — a couple of tactical notes from the close playbook that should fold into the MAP:

1) Lock an internal pre-brief at T-2 business days with Marissa (CS) + engineering lead so the EB is a decision-focused meeting, not discovery.
2) Map evaluation milestones to a single procurement gating item (PO timeline or budget approval) — reduces exec cognitive load.
3) Add fallback EB options: smaller exec-only 30m or broader stakeholder 60m (we should send both invites).

Proposed timeline (high level):
- 5/10–5/14: Tech dry run(s) + validation tests
- 5/17: Internal pre-brief + engineering readiness check
- 5/20 or 5/21: Exec briefing (primary)
- 5/24–5/28: Procurement finalize (PO/contract signature)

Marissa — can you take point on the pre-brief scheduling and attendee list? Alex — can you confirm who from Horizon will need a pre-brief (Jordan called out security)?
